items.claim: LAPS deployment in a domain is visible twice: as a GPO whose DisplayName matches laps, and as every computer object carrying the ms-Mcs-AdmPwdExpirationTime attribute, and the backing Registry.pol is retrievable from the predictable SYSVOL Policies path once the GPO GUID is known.
items.body:
LAPS deployment in a domain is visible twice: as a GPO whose DisplayName matches laps, and as every computer object carrying the ms-Mcs-AdmPwdExpirationTime attribute, and the backing Registry.pol is retrievable from the predictable SYSVOL Policies path once the GPO GUID is known.

HackTricks reference: 15a098c3 (notion:15a098c3-95c5-8082-aff6-c32fcde37e44)
items.disproof: No GPO matches the laps name and no computer object carries ms-Mcs-AdmPwdExpirationTime, or the SYSVOL Policies path is not readable, showing LAPS is not deployed or not exposed.

sources.quote:
page 15a098c3-95c5-8082-aff6-c32fcde37e44

Enumerating LAPS.

powershell Get-DomainGPO | ? { $_.DisplayName -like "*laps*" } | select DisplayName, Name, GPCFileSysPath | fl

image.png

Now enumerating computers that have LAPS.

powershell Get-DomainComputer | ? { $_."ms-Mcs-AdmPwdExpirationTime" -ne $null } | select dnsHostName

image.png

Now let’s download the LAPS policy file,

download \\dev.cyberbotic.io\SysVol\dev.cyberbotic.io\Policies\{2BE4337D-D231-4D23-A029-7B999885E659}\Machine\Registry.pol

Now let’s pars the file.

Group policy allows for centralized management of user and computer settings in Active Directory (AD). GPOs are containers for group policy settings made up of files stored within a predictable network path \ \SYSVOL\ \Policies\ .
A GPO is a virtual collection of policy settings, security permissions, and scope of management (SOM) that you can apply to users and computers in AD.
